issues.legal_issue: The agrarian reform law constitutes genuine agrarian reform protected from challenges under the constitutional guarantees concerning equality, freedom and property.
material_facts: The law vested in the State land that was not in the owner's personal cultivation and land held in personal cultivation above a ceiling.
It provided for State disposal of surplus land and its equitable distribution to tillers for personal cultivation, subject to a ceiling.
The petitioners challenged the law's validity, including the adequacy of compensation and its effects on landowners.
issues.conclusion: The law provides a definite programme of agrarian reform and is protected by Article 31A as applicable to the State; the challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31 therefore fail.
issues.legal_principle: A law must disclose a genuine scheme of agrarian reform to receive Article 31A protection; its title alone is not decisive. When Article 31A applies, challenges under Articles 14, 19 and 31 are unavailable. The Court relied on Kavalappara Kottarathil Kochuni v. State of Madras, Ranjit Singh v. State of Punjab, State of Uttar Pradesh v. Raja Anand Brahma Shah, Kannan Devan Hills Produce v. State of Kerala, and State of Kerala v. Gwalior Rayon Silk Mfg. (Wvg.) Co. Ltd.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_ref: The proceeding challenges the constitutional validity of a law presented as an agrarian reform measure.
predicates.law_takes_nonpersonally_cultivated_land: The law transfers to the State land that its owner does not personally cultivate.
predicates.law_limits_personally_cultivated_holding: The law transfers to the State personally cultivated land held above a specified ceiling.
predicates.law_provides_for_surplus_distribution_to: The law provides for surplus land to be distributed to tillers for personal cultivation, subject to a ceiling.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a reform law that takes non-personally cultivated land, limits personally cultivated holdings, and provides for surplus distribution to tillers, the challenge is barred.

issues.legal_issue: Excluding orchards from the ordinary definition of land while treating them separately does not unreasonably discriminate in favour of orchard owners.
material_facts: The law excluded qualifying orchards from its definition of land but counted land and orchards together when determining the ceiling.
It imposed an annual tax on orchard area exceeding the ceiling.
An orchard was defined as a compact area with enough fruit trees to preclude its use for another agricultural purpose, and orchards had special significance in the State.
Earlier land-reform legislation had also treated orchards separately from other land.
issues.conclusion: The separate treatment of orchards is justified by the scheme of the law and the distinctive nature and significance of orchards; it is not unreasonable discrimination in favour of orchard owners.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not prohibit differential treatment justified by the subject matter and scheme of the legislation. The Court relied on the provisions defining land and orchards, counting both for the ceiling, and taxing excess orchard area, as well as section 4(2) of the Big Landed Estates Abolition Act, which had excluded orchards from the relevant extinguishment provision.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_reform_law and orchards_excluded_from_ordinary_land_definition and orchards_counted_toward_ceiling and excess_orchard_area_subject_to_tax and orchard_character_limits_other_agricultural_use

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_agrarian_ref: The proceeding challenges the constitutional validity of a law presented as an agrarian reform measure.
predicates.orchards_excluded_from_ordinary_land_def: The law treats qualifying orchards separately from land under its ordinary definition.
predicates.orchards_counted_toward_ceiling: The law counts orchard holdings together with other land when fixing the holding ceiling.
predicates.excess_orchard_area_subject_to_tax: The law imposes a tax on orchard area held above the ceiling.
predicates.orchard_character_limits_other_agricultu: The orchard consists of fruit trees in such density that the land is precluded from other agricultural use.

issues.definition: When a challenged reform law separately classifies orchards but counts them toward the ceiling, taxes excess orchard area, and the orchard's character limits other agricultural use, that distinction is not unreasonably discriminatory.
